new_quiz.q: What is a reference board?
choices: A list of the assets in your project
One image that holds a group of pictures you collected to guide your work
A level where you test your materials
A panel in the editor that shows your bookmarks
new_quiz.explain: A reference board puts your collected pictures side by side in one image. You look at it while you work to stay close to your idea.

new_quiz.q: What is a mood target?
choices: The folder where you save your reference images
The number of lights you plan to use
The brightest light in your scene
The single picture and short description that says how your scene should feel
new_quiz.explain: The mood target is one image plus a few lines. It is the goal that you compare your scene against.

new_quiz.q: How does a mood target help you when you light a scene?
choices: It makes it easier to judge if your lighting is right or wrong
It sets the light values in the engine for you
It makes the scene render faster
It removes the need for a Sky Light
new_quiz.explain: Without a target, any lighting can look fine. With a target, you can compare and see what is still different.

new_quiz.q: What do you mark on each image of the reference board?
choices: The size of the image file
The website where you found it
What you are taking from it, such as the light direction or the color
The date when you saved it
new_quiz.explain: Each image is on the board for a reason: the light direction, the color, the material or the composition. The label reminds you which part to copy.

new_quiz.q: What is the key light of a scene?
choices: The light that is placed first
The main light in the scene
The light that casts no shadows
The light with the coldest color
new_quiz.explain: The key light is the main light. Its color and direction decide most of the look, which is why one of your three lines describes it.

new_quiz.q: Which three things do the 3 lines of your mood target give?
choices: The time of day, the color of the key light and the feeling you want
The engine version, the template and the level name
The camera, the lens and the resolution
The number of images, their sizes and their sources
new_quiz.explain: One line is for the time of day, one for the color of the key light, and one for the feeling. Together they describe the target in words.

new_quiz.q: Why does the sky have a strong effect on the mood of a scene?
choices: It hides the objects on the ground
It sets how fast the scene renders
It gives a base color to everything below it
It decides which materials you can use
new_quiz.explain: Light from the sky falls on every surface. Its color becomes the base color of the whole scene, so it shapes the mood.

new_quiz.q: What is an HDRI?
choices: A 360 degree photo of a real sky that also lights the scene
A light that only shines in one direction
A fog actor that reacts to light
A file that describes the shape of light from a lamp
new_quiz.explain: An HDRI is a photo that covers all directions and stores a wide range of brightness. It can be shown as the sky and used as the light of the scene.

new_quiz.q: How does the atmosphere system make a sky?
choices: It plays a video of clouds
It copies the colors of the floor
It loads a photo from the Content Browser
It calculates the sky from a sun light
new_quiz.explain: Sky Atmosphere works together with the Directional Light. When you change the sun angle, the color of the sky changes with it.

new_quiz.q: What does a Sky Light do?
choices: It casts sharp shadows like the sun
It gives soft light that comes from the whole sky
It lights one small spot like a lamp
It adds fog near the ground
new_quiz.explain: A Sky Light lights the scene softly from all directions of the sky. It fills the shadows that the sun does not reach.

new_quiz.q: You want to use the HDRI Backdrop actor but cannot find it. What do you check first?
choices: That the level has a Sky Atmosphere
That the Directional Light is deleted
That the HDRI Backdrop plugin is enabled in Edit, then Plugins
That the project uses the Third Person template
new_quiz.explain: The HDRI Backdrop actor comes from the HDRI Backdrop plugin. The plugin also brings a sample HDRI you can use.

new_quiz.q: Why do you compare the two versions from the same camera bookmark?
choices: So both pictures show exactly the same view
So both levels use the same fog color
So the HDRI is loaded only once
So the screenshots have a higher resolution
new_quiz.explain: If the view is the same, the only difference between the pictures is the sky setup. That makes the comparison fair.

new_quiz.q: What is an IES profile?
choices: A setting that locks the exposure of the camera
A material that makes a lamp glow
A list of all lights in the level
A small file from a lamp maker that describes the shape of the light of a real lamp
new_quiz.explain: An IES profile holds measured data about how a real lamp spreads its light. Applied to a light in Unreal, it gives that light the same pattern.

new_quiz.q: In which unit do you set the color temperature of a light?
choices: Candela
Kelvin
Lumens
Degrees
new_quiz.explain: Color temperature is measured in Kelvin. Candela and lumens are units for how strong a light is.

new_quiz.q: Why do you set the exposure to a fixed value before you judge the brightness of your lights?
choices: A fixed exposure stops Unreal from adjusting the picture, so you can see brightness changes
A fixed exposure makes all lights use the same color
A fixed exposure turns off the shadows of the lights
A fixed exposure makes the IES profile load faster
new_quiz.explain: Exposure is how bright the camera makes the picture. If it adjusts by itself, a stronger light does not look brighter, so you cannot compare values.

new_quiz.q: How do you bring an IES file from a lamp maker into your project?
choices: Type its name in the Outliner
Open it in the Material Editor
Drag the .ies file into the Content Browser
Copy it into the Details panel
new_quiz.explain: Dragging the .ies file into the Content Browser imports it as an asset. After that you can pick it on a light.

new_quiz.q: Where do you apply an imported IES profile to a light?
choices: In the Exposure section of the Post Process Volume
In the Light Color setting of the light
In the World Settings of the level
In the IES Texture setting of the light
new_quiz.explain: You select the light and pick the profile in its IES Texture setting. The light then follows the shape stored in the profile.

new_quiz.q: What is the gain of lighting a room with real-world values?
choices: The room needs no Post Process Volume
The lighting behaves in a way you can predict
The lights no longer cost performance
The room looks the same at every exposure
new_quiz.explain: Real values, such as the candela or lumens of a real lamp, make lights behave like the lamps you know. Your scenes also stay consistent with each other.

new_quiz.q: What is composition?
choices: The way things are arranged inside the picture frame
The number of lights in a scene
The list of materials on a mesh
The order in which actors are loaded
new_quiz.explain: Composition is about what is in the frame and where. The camera position decides it, so it matters as much as the lighting.

new_quiz.q: What is a Cine Camera Actor?
choices: A tool that records the screen to a video file
A camera that follows the player in the game
A camera in Unreal that works like a real film camera
A bookmark that stores a camera position
new_quiz.explain: A Cine Camera Actor has the settings of a real film camera, such as a focal length and a focus distance.

new_quiz.q: What does the focal length of a Cine Camera Actor control?
choices: How bright the picture is
How wide or narrow the view is
How fast the camera moves
How many frames are saved
new_quiz.explain: A short focal length gives a wide view and a long focal length gives a narrow view.

new_quiz.q: What does it mean to pilot a camera?
choices: You attach the camera to the player character
You lock the camera so that it cannot move
You copy the camera to another level
You look through the camera and move it
new_quiz.explain: While you pilot a camera, the viewport shows its view and your viewport movement moves the camera. This is how you frame a shot.

new_quiz.q: What do you use a composition overlay such as the rule of thirds grid for?
choices: To change the focal length
To save a camera bookmark
To adjust the frame
To raise the screenshot resolution
new_quiz.explain: The overlay draws guide lines over the view. You move the camera until the important things sit well on those lines.

new_quiz.q: Which three views do you save as camera bookmarks?
choices: One wide view, one medium view and one detail view
One top view, one front view and one side view
One day view, one night view and one fog view
One lit view, one unlit view and one wireframe view
new_quiz.explain: Wide, medium and detail views show the scene at three distances. Saved bookmarks let you return to exactly the same views later.

new_quiz.q: What is a diorama?
choices: A large open world with many levels
A small, complete scene, like a model in a box
A flat image that is used as a sky
A camera that works like a film camera
new_quiz.explain: A diorama is small but complete. Here it is a piece of landscape of roughly 10 x 10 m with plants and finished lighting.

new_quiz.q: Why does a small finished scene teach you more than a big scene you never finish?
choices: A small scene needs no lighting
A small scene can be built without a target
A small scene is not judged by anyone
You have to make every part work together
new_quiz.explain: Finishing forces you to connect terrain, plants, light, exposure and camera. In an unfinished scene you never reach that step.

new_quiz.q: In which editor mode do you paint plants or rocks onto the landscape of the diorama?
choices: Foliage Mode
Modeling Mode
Selection Mode
Animation Mode
new_quiz.explain: Foliage Mode paints many copies of a mesh, such as plants or rocks, onto a surface. Landscape Mode is where you create and sculpt the terrain.

new_quiz.q: In which units do you set the intensity of the local light in the diorama?
choices: Kelvin or degrees
Meters or centimeters
Candela or lumens
Percent or pixels
new_quiz.explain: Candela and lumens are real units for the strength of a light. Using them makes a Point Light behave like a real lamp.

new_quiz.q: Why do you set Metering Mode to Manual in a Post Process Volume for the diorama?
choices: So the fog becomes volumetric
So the exposure is your choice and not the default
So the camera bookmarks are saved
So the landscape can be sculpted
new_quiz.explain: With Manual metering the brightness of the picture stays where you set it. Infinite Extent (Unbound) makes the volume apply to the whole level.

new_quiz.q: What do the 3 lines of your writeup say?
choices: Which plugins you enabled
How long each step took
Which meshes you painted
What matches the target and what does not match it yet
new_quiz.explain: You judge the diorama against your mood target. Naming what matches and what does not is how you find the next thing to improve.

new_quiz.q: What are light shafts?
choices: Beams of light that you can see in the air
Shadows that fall on the floor
Lamps that hang from a ceiling
Reflections on a wet surface
new_quiz.explain: Volumetric Fog makes light visible in the air. When light comes through a window, you see it as beams, often called light shafts.

new_quiz.q: Where do you turn on Volumetric Fog?
choices: In the Details panel of the window mesh
In the Details panel of the Sky Light
In the Details panel of the Exponential Height Fog actor
In the Details panel of the Post Process Volume
new_quiz.explain: Volumetric Fog is an option of the Exponential Height Fog actor. The level needs this actor before any light shafts can appear.

new_quiz.q: The level has no Exponential Height Fog actor. Where do you find one?
choices: In the Content Browser, under Add
In the Place Actors panel, under Visual Effects
In Edit, then Plugins
In the view mode menu of the viewport
new_quiz.explain: Exponential Height Fog is in the Visual Effects group of the Place Actors panel. You drag it into the level.

new_quiz.q: Which setting of a light controls how strongly that light shows in the fog?
choices: Source Angle
Attenuation Radius
IES Texture
Volumetric Scattering Intensity
new_quiz.explain: Volumetric Scattering Intensity is in the Details panel of the light. A higher value makes the shafts of that light stronger.

new_quiz.q: The light shafts are so strong that the room looks milky. What do you change first?
choices: Raise the Intensity of the light
Lower Volumetric Scattering Intensity on the light
Delete the window from the wall
Turn off shadows on the light
new_quiz.explain: The shafts should support the image and not wash it out. Lowering Volumetric Scattering Intensity makes that light show less in the fog.

new_quiz.q: Which lights do you aim through the window to make the shafts?
choices: A Sky Light or a Rect Light
A Point Light or a Sky Light
A Directional Light or a Spot Light
A Rect Light or a Point Light
new_quiz.explain: A Directional Light or a Spot Light sends light in one direction. Aimed through the gap in the wall, it forms clear beams in the fog.

new_quiz.q: How is a Local Fog Volume different from the height fog of a level?
choices: It only works at night
It only works indoors
It is a small area of fog you can place anywhere
It covers the whole scene at once
new_quiz.explain: Height fog covers the whole scene. A Local Fog Volume adds fog in one place, so you control exactly where it is.

new_quiz.q: Why do layers of fog at different distances make a picture look deeper?
choices: Far things become softer than near things
Far things become larger than near things
Near things become darker than far things
Near things lose their shadows
new_quiz.explain: More fog lies between the camera and far objects, so they look softer. The eye reads that difference as distance.

new_quiz.q: Where do you place the two Local Fog Volumes?
choices: Both in front of the camera
Both inside the main subject
Both above the sky
So that they separate the foreground from the background
new_quiz.explain: For example, one sits behind the main subject and one far away. The subject then stands out clearly from what is behind it.

new_quiz.q: What shape does the fog of a Local Fog Volume have?
choices: A flat sheet that lies on the ground
A sphere that fades out toward its edge
A box with hard edges
A cone that points at the camera
new_quiz.explain: A Local Fog Volume holds a round area of fog that fades out from the center. That soft edge lets it blend into the scene.

new_quiz.q: Which values do you change to make the fog of a Local Fog Volume thicker or thinner?
choices: The two Extinction values in the Details panel
The two Mobility values in the Details panel
The Source Angle and the Intensity
The Inner Radius and the Falloff Distance
new_quiz.explain: The Extinction values set how dense the fog is. Higher values give thicker fog and lower values give thinner fog.

new_quiz.q: Why do you take the two screenshots from the same view?
choices: So the fog volumes are saved with the level
So the file names are the same
So the only difference between them is the fog
So the screenshots are taken faster
new_quiz.explain: A before and after pair is only useful if nothing else changes. With the same view, you see exactly what the volumes add.

new_quiz.q: What does the angle of the sun decide?
choices: Which materials the objects use
How many objects cast shadows
How soft the edges of the shadows are
Where shadows fall and how long they are
new_quiz.explain: A low sun gives long shadows and a high sun gives short ones. The direction of the sun decides where they fall.

new_quiz.q: What does the Source Angle setting of the Directional Light decide?
choices: The color of the sunlight
How soft the edges of the shadows are
The height of the sun in the sky
How far the shadows are drawn
new_quiz.explain: Source Angle is the size of the light source as seen from the scene. A larger source gives softer shadow edges.

new_quiz.q: Which shadows does a small Source Angle value give?
choices: Sharp shadows
Soft shadows
No shadows
Blue shadows
new_quiz.explain: A small value gives sharp shadows, and a large value gives soft shadows.

new_quiz.q: How do you change the sun angle in the level?
choices: Move the Directional Light higher
Scale the Directional Light
Rotate the Directional Light
Rename the Directional Light
new_quiz.explain: A Directional Light shines in one direction over the whole level. Only its rotation matters, so you rotate it to change the sun angle.

new_quiz.q: Where do you find Source Angle?
choices: In the World Settings, under Lightmass
In the Details panel of the Sky Light, under Light
In the view mode menu of the viewport
In the Details panel of the Directional Light, under Light
new_quiz.explain: Source Angle is a property of the Directional Light. You select the light and look under Light in the Details panel.

new_quiz.q: What is a contact sheet?
choices: A list of the lights in the level
One image that shows all the renders together
A text file with the sun angles
A folder that holds the screenshots
new_quiz.explain: A contact sheet puts all six renders in one image. Side by side, it is easy to see where the shapes are the easiest to read.
